topic:
The statistical price of corrupted records under weak causal overlap. Fix d>=1, alpha,beta,kappa>0, L>=4. Clean observations O=(X,A,Y) lie in [0,1]^d x {0,1} x [0,1]. Under P, X is exactly uniform, e(x)=P(A=1|X=x)=x_1^kappa u(x), u in H^alpha(L) with 1/4<=u<=1/2, and mu_a(x)=E[Y|X=x,A=a] in H^beta(L) with 1/4<=mu_a<=3/4. Conditional outcome laws otherwise unrestricted. H^s(L) bounds all partial derivatives through m=ceil(s)-1 by L and order-m derivatives have (s-m)-Holder seminorm <=L under sup norm. At the boundary x_1=0, mu_1 is its unique continuous extension, not an independently identified conditional value. Clean consistency and conditional exchangeability identify theta(P)=integral_[0,1]^d (mu_1-mu_0) dx. Observe n>=2 iid records from R=(1-epsilon)P+epsilon Q, with known 0<=epsilon<=1/10 and Q any probability law on the same record space; Q may corrupt all three fields. Estimator knows d,alpha,beta,kappa,L,epsilon and clean covariate design, but not P,Q,u,mu_a. Fixed nonzero epsilon entails irreducible ambiguity; do not claim point identification of theta from R. For every fixed d,alpha,beta,kappa,L above and jointly for all n>=2 and 0<=epsilon<=1/10, determine an explicit deterministic evaluable rate rho(n,epsilon;d,alpha,beta,kappa,L), including logarithms at regime boundaries, such that c*rho <= inf_T sup_(P,Q) E_((1-epsilon)P+epsilon Q)^n |T-theta(P)| <= C*rho, over all Borel data-only estimators and exactly the declared clean-law/contamination class. Constants c,C may depend on the fixed class parameters but not n,epsilon. Supply a total finite computable attaining estimator with stated computation, and matching same-experiment converses. Derive the joint clean-functional, overlap and contamination transitions from primitives; resolve whether clean risk and the ATE total-variation modulus can be attained simultaneously or whether nuisance learning incurs an additional interaction penalty. Neither the max formula, an interaction, nor an exponent is assumed. A whole-law TV estimation bound, oracle known-nuisance rate, one-point contamination modulus or unmatched clipping bound alone does not discharge the kernel. Consumer: Sasaki and Ura (2022), Average treatment effect estimates robust to the limited overlap problem: robustate, Stata Journal, and its right-heart-catheterization analysis. The result separates robustness to limited overlap from robustness to corrupted records and provides an error-radius and trimming/boundary-correction benchmark when a fraction of records is unreliable. This is a theoretical benchmark on a known-design boundary class, not a claim that the published parametric-propensity workflow satisfies this class or that its actual data are corrupted. https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/1536867X221106402 PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The presolve derives the clean-ATE total-variation modulus delta^((beta+1)/(beta+kappa+1)), including changing propensity. On the full d=1, alpha=beta=1, kappa=2 class, unknown-nuisance cell means with variable widths and boundary extrapolation give the matched candidate rate n^(-2/5)+sqrt(epsilon). The draft supplies population bias, arbitrary full-record contamination, random-denominator and empty-cell arguments; exact witness and dyadic calculations were checked. These are unverified derivations, not the general theorem. A projected nuisance-product identity isolates the potential fast-functional gain, but naive pair correction incurs an explicit epsilon^2 times kernel-diagonal bias under concentrated contamination. Current comparisons did not identify a full-frontier collision; a 2024 robust-functional conference talk remains a literature lead to resolve.
UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Construct a finite robust projected correction with nuisance pilots and Gram matrix learned from corrupted records at resolutions above stable local occupancy, or prove a matching interaction penalty; complete the same-class converse and transition logarithms.
EARLY KILL TEST: Test the proposed correction on the exact finite-cell slab with a point contaminant and then diffuse contamination within one fine cell. Without a proved bound preserving the clean high-resolution gain or a matched interaction lower bound, abandon that estimator route. The solved Lipschitz regime must remain a consistency check.
STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/stat_corrupted_ate_overlap_nuisance_frontier.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the full minimax absolute-error phase diagram for the bounded-outcome Hölder ATE under one-sided polynomial overlap and full-record Huber contamination, including whether an additional nuisance-contamination interaction term appears.

source_refs.claim: Shows that treatment-effect estimation with unbounded inverse weights is irregular and that rates depend on propensity-tail behavior.
source_refs.author: Shakeeb Khan and Elie Tamer

source_refs.claim: Derives general Huber-contamination lower bounds through a total-variation modulus and upper bounds via robust testing, without specializing them to weak-overlap causal functionals.
source_refs.author: Mengjie Chen, Chao Gao, and Zhao Ren

source_refs.claim: Develops bias-corrected trimming for ATE estimation under limited overlap and illustrates it with right-heart-catheterization data, but does not study adversarial record corruption.
source_refs.author: Yuya Sasaki and Takuya Ura

source_refs.claim: Constructs density-power IPW and doubly robust estimators for outcome outliers under stronger overlap and narrower contamination than arbitrary corruption of X, A, and Y.
source_refs.author: Kazuharu Harada and Hironori Fujisawa

source_refs.excerpt: Adaptation to unknown calibration, bounded-outcome variants, arbitrary shell constants ... remain open.
For κ>0, claim only the proved first-order bracket and leave the higher-order rate ... open.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Clean weak-overlap work derives irregular limits, trimming corrections, or restricted smooth-function frontiers, while causal outlier work assumes stronger overlap or narrower contamination. Generic Huber theory supplies a total-variation modulus but neither the clean functional rate nor a computable causal estimator. Prior CausalSmith work additionally leaves the unknown-propensity higher-order frontier unresolved at a spatial overlap zero. The missing step is a contaminated orthogonal or higher-order remainder analysis for nuisance pilots learned in low-occupancy shells; those remainders may exceed both the clean minimax rate and the one-law contamination modulus.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit piecewise rate rho(n,epsilon;d,alpha,beta,kappa,L), including all boundary logarithms, with a finite attaining estimator, matching same-experiment lower bounds, and a theorem deciding whether rho is max{rho_clean,omega_TV(epsilon)} or contains a quantified interaction term.

writing_exemplar.why: Its applied framing cleanly separates the full-population ATE target from instability caused by limited overlap, which can be extended to distinguish overlap robustness from record-corruption robustness.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: ATE weighting needs comparable treated and control records -> weak overlap creates unstable small denominators -> trimming and boundary correction address overlap instability -> quantify the additional information-theoretic price of unreliable complete records

method_exemplars.technique: Use robust testing and the total-variation modulus to turn clean-experiment separation into contamination-aware minimax upper and lower bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired phase diagram must reconcile clean functional difficulty with indistinguishability of clean laws whose Huber neighborhoods intersect.

method_exemplars.technique: Use projection-based higher-order influence-function U-statistics and an explicit truncation-dimension bias-variance calculation for missing-response means.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The treated potential-outcome mean is a missing-response functional, and first-order nuisance products may obscure its faster clean functional rate.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its minimax decomposition for a global ATE with multiple nuisance functions, including higher-order correction and nuisance-product lower bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target is likewise a global ATE functional whose rate may exceed direct nuisance-learning rates, but weak overlap and contamination alter every remainder channel.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct a finite robust projected-correction estimator whose nuisance pilots and projection Gram matrix are learned from corrupted weak-overlap records without losing the clean high-resolution ATE gain, or prove that such preservation is impossible.

source_refs.claim: Introduces projection-based higher-order estimating equations attaining optimal rates for missing-response means under low nuisance regularity.
source_refs.author: James Robins, Lingling Li, Rajarshi Mukherjee, Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen, and Aad van der Vaart

source_refs.claim: Shows that even a tractable robust extension of a doubly robust ATE equation requires an additional bias correction.
source_refs.author: Kazuharu Harada and Hironori Fujisawa

source_refs.claim: Develops minimum-distance estimators using generalized resilience under total-variation corruption, but not higher-order causal U-statistics with vanishing propensities.
source_refs.author: Banghua Zhu, Jiantao Jiao, and Jacob Steinhardt

source_refs.excerpt: At κ=0 use finite-dimensional projection U-statistic corrections to both matrix and vector moments.
a shared Rademacher prior creates nonzero two-observation cross terms

open_problems.why_unsolved: Clean higher-order proofs first control an empirical projection operator and then exploit degeneracy of a pairwise correction. Arbitrary corruption of X, A, and Y breaks both steps: contaminants can leverage the empirical Gram matrix, alter both kernel arguments, destroy conditional degeneracy, and create an epsilon-squared same-cell or diagonal bias. Weak overlap simultaneously prevents arbitrarily fine treated-cell occupancy. Existing robust semiparametric estimators control first-order influence, while generalized-resilience methods do not preserve the cancellation structure of projected causal U-statistics.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A completely specified finite estimator with robust pilots, a stabilized robust Gram operator, and a projected correction whose contaminated pilot, operator, off-diagonal, diagonal, and occupancy errors are uniformly bounded at the clean higher-order resolution, or a matching lower bound for the exact additional penalty.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation separates ordinary double robustness from resistance to actual outliers and explains why naive robustification loses bias cancellation.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: IPW and doubly robust scores amplify aberrant observations -> bounded or density-power weighting limits first-order influence -> naive robustification loses nuisance cancellation -> design a robust higher-order correction that preserves functional-rate gains

method_exemplars.technique: Use empirical higher-order influence functions with an estimated projection kernel and prove that operator-estimation error remains below the corrected functional rate.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both estimators must learn a finite Gram operator and use it inside a pair correction for an average causal functional.

method_exemplars.technique: Use generalized resilience and weakened-discrepancy minimum-distance projection to control empirical and population effects of arbitrary total-variation perturbations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Robust learning of projection coefficients and Gram moments requires a multivariate moment-stability device before higher-order cancellation can be invoked.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the Hoeffding decomposition and separate concentration analysis for linear, degenerate, and diagonal components of a localized U-statistic.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed kill test turns on controlling these exact components after a point contaminant or diffuse within-cell contamination is introduced.

open_problems.open_problem: Build a matching same-experiment converse using full-support Hölder clean laws whose Huber neighborhoods intersect and whose ATE separation jointly realizes the overlap, nuisance-product, and contamination obstructions.

source_refs.excerpt: Replace the two-reservoir lower-bound witness with a construction valid without ... richness inequalities.
one-observation mixture cancellation does not control the shared-prior product experiment
the discharged core supports only a parametric lower floor plus estimator-side achievability

open_problems.why_unsolved: Prior clean ATE attempts either lacked a shell-matching lower bound or required reservoir-richness inequalities absent from the declared class. A separate smooth-nuisance lineage shows that matching one-observation mixtures does not control shared-prior product experiments. Contamination imposes another exact condition: admissible Q0 and Q1 must make the observed mixtures identical or sufficiently testing-close while exact-uniform X, the x1^kappa u(x) propensity form, Hölder radii, and bounded outcomes remain valid. Oracle or whole-law surrogate lower bounds do not establish this same-experiment claim.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite collection of explicit clean-law pairs or fuzzy priors and contaminating laws with identical or testing-close observed n-sample experiments, verified membership in the declared class, and ATE separation matching every asserted rate component and transition case.

writing_exemplar.why: Its support-and-tail narrative is a natural model for explaining why mass near a propensity boundary determines the hard statistical experiment.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Weak support makes treatment-effect estimation irregular -> quantitative tail mass determines attainable separation -> existing hard families require extra reservoir geometry -> construct legal contamination-colliding alternatives on the exact boundary class

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the two-convex-mixture lower-bound method and fixed-product Hellinger calculation for coordinated perturbations of multiple nuisances.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The converse must hide an ATE shift through simultaneous propensity and outcome perturbations while controlling the actual n-fold observed experiment.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over explicit hard subexperiments sharing public nuisance approximations and localize their target separation to weak-overlap shells.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its nuisance-product lower channels are a close clean ATE analogue, but the destination must additionally enforce Hölder geometry and Huber-neighborhood collision.

method_exemplars.technique: Use localized fuzzy hypotheses with calibrated propensity and regression bumps and an explicit product-likelihood bound.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies a structurally analogous smooth-nuisance converse whose support construction must be replaced on an exactly uniform design.

open_problems.open_problem: For a known contaminated law R and known epsilon, characterize the sharp identified interval for the clean-law ATE over the Hölder boundary-overlap class and determine when its diameter equals the ATE total-variation modulus.

source_refs.claim: Shows that parameters are generally not point identified under contaminated sampling and develops identified bounds instead of robust point estimates.
source_refs.author: Joel L. Horowitz and Charles F. Manski

source_refs.claim: Connects Huber-contamination lower bounds to the largest parameter separation among clean laws within a small total-variation distance.
source_refs.author: Mengjie Chen, Chao Gao, and Zhao Ren

source_refs.claim: Derives ATE bounds under genuine non-overlap using an overlap-region effect and bounded extrapolation outside it, but assumes clean observations.
source_refs.author: Herbert P. Susmann, Alec McClean, and Iván Díaz

open_problems.why_unsolved: Generic contamination bounds do not exploit exact-uniform covariates, e(x)=x1^kappa u(x), or the coupled Hölder restrictions on propensity and outcome regressions. Conversely, recent non-overlap bounds assume clean observations and do not allow Q to alter covariates and treatment labels. Although clean overlap fails only on a null boundary, fixed epsilon makes R=(1-epsilon)P+epsilon Q nonunique; sharpness therefore requires solving a constrained smooth-law decontamination problem rather than applying ordinary Manski missing-mass bounds.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit variational or finite-dimensional limiting characterization of infimum and supremum ATE over all class-conforming P dominated by R/(1-epsilon), with sharp extremizers and a theorem relating worst-case interval diameter to the total-variation modulus across beta-kappa regimes.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the correct conceptual pivot from point estimation of an unidentified clean parameter to estimation of contamination-compatible bounds.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Data errors make the clean distribution nonunique -> the clean parameter is not point identified -> robust point estimates obscure this ambiguity -> characterize the sharp clean-ATE interval under causal smoothness and weak overlap

method_exemplars.technique: Translate mixture compatibility into domination and mass-allocation constraints, then optimize the target functional over admissible clean distributions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired endpoints are contamination-identified extrema with additional causal and Hölder restrictions sharpening the generic construction.

method_exemplars.technique: Decompose an ATE bound into an estimable overlap component and bounded extrapolation component, smooth nonsmooth endpoints, and apply debiased estimation with multiplier bootstrap inference.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its endpoints are causal ATE bounds driven by scarce treatment support, providing an estimation template after the contamination-compatible endpoints are characterized.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the total-variation modulus and exact indistinguishability of intersecting Huber neighborhoods to construct extremal clean-law pairs.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This directly links the sharp identified-set diameter to the contamination term in minimax estimation.

open_problems.open_problem: Solve the exact finite-cell boundary-slab ATE problem with simultaneously rare treatment cells and arbitrary full-record contamination by robustifying the clean heavy-light polynomial estimator.

source_refs.excerpt: The run completed the computable hybrid-estimator upper bound, light-cell approximation-and-variance lemma.
Treatment-arm rarity and covariate-cell rarity interact inside factorial-moment variances.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The accepted hybrid estimator is proved for clean multinomial records with fixed interior overlap. In a boundary slab, covariate-cell rarity and treated-arm rarity coincide, while arbitrary Q can manufacture pilot counts and corrupt every factorial-moment input. Its heavy-light classification and unbiased polynomial lifts are therefore no longer controlled. The first proof step that changes is the light-cell approximation-and-variance lemma, which must become a robust moment lemma uniform in the smallest treated-cell mass and must be paired with a contaminated multinomial lower experiment.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite-alphabet minimax theorem giving explicit risk in sample size, cell masses, treatment probabilities, and epsilon, attained by a total robust heavy-light polynomial estimator and matched by a contaminated multinomial converse for both point and diffuse within-cell contaminants.

writing_exemplar.why: Its sparse-cell ATE formulation makes occupancy the central statistical obstacle and provides a natural setup for the finite-slab kill test.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Discrete confounding creates many sparse causal cells -> polynomial moments recover a global ATE beyond plug-in limits -> rare treatment further reduces arm-specific occupancy -> adversarial records require a robust joint cell-and-overlap frontier

method_exemplars.technique: Use best-polynomial approximation with factorial-moment lifting and separate sparse from dense cells in the risk proof.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired finite estimator targets a rational cell functional through rare-cell moments but must replace unbiased lifts with contamination-stable analogues.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the moment-matching lower prior and its reduction from one-arm mean estimation to the ATE.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The finite-slab converse needs the same causal cell geometry while additionally matching weak treatment probabilities and intersecting contamination neighborhoods.

method_exemplars.technique: Relate factorial-moment polynomial correction to empirical projection-kernel correction through their common finite-dimensional moment operator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This correspondence determines whether a robust finite-cell solution can serve as the local module for the continuous Hölder estimator.

literature_map:
Khan and Tamer (2010, Econometrica) establish that inverse-weight identification can be irregular when weights diverge; rates depend on propensity-tail behavior.
Crump et al. (2009, Biometrika) optimize trimming by changing the target population, illustrating the estimand-versus-stability tradeoff.
Ma and Wang (2020, JASA) derive Gaussian and non-Gaussian trimmed-IPW limits and correct trimming bias, but assume clean records.
Sasaki and Ura (2022, Econometric Theory) extend bias correction to ratio moments; their robustate article carries this weak-overlap logic to right-heart catheterization.
Rothe (2017, Econometrica) shows that limited overlap distorts coverage through tiny local sample sizes, motivating nonstandard confidence procedures.
Dorn (2025, arXiv:2504.13273) studies thresholded AIPW with learned nuisances and shows how weak overlap changes nuisance-rate requirements and limit theory.
Harada and Fujisawa (2024, Statistica Sinica) robustify IPW and doubly robust estimation against outcome outliers but require an extra bias correction and substantially stronger overlap and contamination structure.
Cantoni and de Luna (2020, Econometrics and Statistics) combine missing-data weighting with bounded-influence semiparametric estimation, emphasizing that weighting amplifies contamination.
Lee et al. (2025, arXiv:2507.17439) propose bounded-influence and covariate-balancing ATE inference without the nonparametric weak-overlap Huber minimax frontier.
Chen, Gao, and Ren (2016, EJS) provide the clean-risk-versus-TV-modulus template for Huber minimax theory, though their generic construction does not exploit causal functional structure.
Robins et al. (2017, Annals of Statistics) provide projection-based higher-order U-statistics for low-regularity missing-response means; arbitrary contamination breaks Gram concentration and U-statistic cancellation.
Zhu, Jiao, and Steinhardt (2022, Annals of Statistics) develop generalized-resilience estimators under TV corruption but do not treat contaminated higher-order causal corrections.
Horowitz and Manski (1995, Econometrica) establish the partial-identification perspective for contaminated sampling, while the smooth weak-overlap sharpening remains unresolved.
Susmann, McClean, and Díaz (2025, arXiv:2509.20206) derive clean-data ATE bounds under non-overlap, providing an adjacent endpoint-inference template.
The scan located no paper deriving the joint n, epsilon, d, alpha, beta, and kappa frontier, preserving higher-order functional gains under arbitrary full-record corruption, or proving a matching interaction penalty.
